mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, investors anticipate future rate hikes, reducing risk premia and pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the following 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the next month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger period (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not rise by >0.25pp in the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in PAYEMS (labor market activity) of at least 2% over the next month coincides with rising corporate hiring confidence, which elevates expected future profits and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2% over the next month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during the PAYEMS up-move, or hiring momentum decays before the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) unexpectedly exceeds prior month by more than 5% and is sustained for two consecutive months, it signals resilient consumer demand, which supports higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >5% in month t and again in month t+1
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive during the double-month HOUST up-move (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 8% in a single month, followed by a rebound of ≥3% in the next month, predicts a temporary supply shock that produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥8% in month t, then rises by ≥3% in month t+1
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during the pattern, or the pattern does not occur as described.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE (labor cost pressure) by at least 0.2 percentage points each for two months indicate a dual disinflationary signal that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls by ≥0.2pp and UNRATE falls by ≥0.2pp in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) during the double decline, or proxies do not meet the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3.5% for three consecutive months, it signals weakening labor market pressures and a shift toward wage moderation, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during the three-month UNRATE decline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in GDPC1 (goods demand) by at least 10% and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 4% in the same quarter predicts strong economic momentum that supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by ≥10% and RSAFS increases by ≥4% in the same quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during the quarter when both proxies rise as specified (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent CPIAUCSL inflation above 4%, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days tend to be negative due to market anticipation of rate hikes and reduced growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% for at least 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the high-inflation period (t-test p > 0.05).
